Mark, it is Tom, calling right after the panel. Short version: I liked her. Here is what stood out. About twenty minutes in, she brought up the vendor contract that fell through last year, and nobody had asked her about it. She put it on the table herself, and then she walked us through the three things she changed afterwards, in about two sentences. Almost nobody does that. Second thing. Dana asked for the total cost of that program, and she did not have the number with her. She held off. She said she would rather send us the real figure the same day than come up with something in the room, and then she moved on. Dana wrote that down, and from Dana that is a compliment. So here is what I need before Friday. Find out whether Ray is going to weigh in, because the VP will not sign off on the offer until the safety side has said something. Push him if you have to. Thanks.

I want to name something I see in almost every senior client who reads English beautifully. On the page they are excellent. The moment they speak, they sound like a document. The reason is simple: they learned this language from documents. A report says raise, generate, approve, encounter. A person in a meeting says bring up, come up with, sign off on, run into. Same meaning, different system. Now, I am not telling you that the long verb is wrong. It is not wrong at all. It is written English, and it will keep serving you in a report or a board paper. But if every verb you speak comes from the page, the room hears distance, and distance is not what you want in an interview. So, two rules. First, do not try to learn a list of two hundred phrasal verbs. Learn eight, and use them until they are yours. Second, watch where the pronoun goes. With a separable verb it goes in the middle. Bring it up. Never bring up it. That one detail is what makes the sentence sound like a person.

We ran into a licensing issue two weeks before the launch. The vendor contract fell through, and the program lost six weeks. The team came up with a workaround in two days. Security weighed in, and my director signed off on it the same week. Today I bring it up in the first two minutes, and then I walk them through what changed.
